- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.6) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., <0.4) — model fails to recognize bearish momentum, leading to lagged corrections.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in trending upticks and too low in downtrends — adjust by smoothing out extremes with recent sentiment-weighted averages.
- Lagged response to sentiment shifts: if sentiment drops sharply, model doesn’t adjust forecast quickly enough — apply a 2–3 day lag correction for sentiment-driven reversals.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history: when sentiment is volatile, don’t extrapolate too far into future — cap forecast range within ±1.5σ of recent 7-day moving average.
- For high-sentiment periods, reduce forecast volatility — model tends to overreact; use sentiment as a dampening factor on price variance.
